faq_intro: Short answers. Each question has its own link.
faq_data_q: Does my data leave the house?
faq_data_a: Not because of the mandate. It is checked by a guard outside the agent – in the intended setup a device in your home – and only a confirmation question goes to your phone. What the agent itself is allowed to read does leave with the agent, so a mandate is also a decision about what it may see.
faq_tricked_q: What if the agent is tricked?
faq_tricked_a: It can still only do what the mandate allows. Critical actions always need an explicit rule or a person.
faq_product_q: Do I need to buy something?
faq_product_a: No. The Home-Mandate Specification is free and open. “Home-Mandate for Home Assistant” is one implementation of it; any other product or open-source project can implement it just as well.
faq_owner_a: No company. The text is CC BY 4.0, the code Apache 2.0, and changes are discussed in public.
faq_no_answer_q: What happens if I don’t answer a question on my phone?
faq_no_answer_a: After the timeout – for example two minutes – the request counts as denied.
faq_matter_q: How does this relate to Matter or Home Assistant?
faq_matter_a: The specification sits above them: it decides whether a command may be sent. Matter or Home Assistant then deliver it.
faq_app_q: Isn’t my smart home app enough?
faq_app_a: It is built for people you trust. A mandate gives every agent limits of its own: single actions, maximum values, times of day, a confirmation on your phone and a log. [Examples from everyday life](/everyday/)
